answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may earn or vote, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud links the account to a fake identity. Creating a hundred accounts no longer gives an attacker a hundred free voices: each must tie up capital, and detection destroys some of it. An island community might use saffron trades to fund checks, while quartz receipts record which stake was forfeited.
